Origin-destination patterns projected by Milwaukee County show that 67 percent of the airport oriented traffic will enter the air terminal facilities via the proposed Airport Spur connection and 33 percent is expected to make use of Howell Avenue. Of this group using Howell Avenue, 22 percent should arrive at the airport entrance road from the north and 11 percent from the south. The projected vehicular traffic that will be using the proposed freeway in 1990 is 19,600 vehicles per day of which 9% would be truck traffic. Thirty percent of the traffic will come from the north on 1-94, 63% from the west on 1-894 and 7% from the south on 1-94.
On site surveys by SEMRPC indicate the ground travel to and from General Mitchell Field consists of more than airline passengers and visitors who are there to meet a passenger or to see him off. It includes persons there for employment and business activity as well as an attraction for sight-seers, diners and tourists for recreational purposes. These studies show that in 1968 the airline traveler constituted less than 1/3 of the total traffic to the airport and that social recreation trips generated 1/5 of the inbound person trips to General Mitchell Field. All these activities necessitate recognition of General Mitchell Field as a major traffic generator.
